title: golang stack corruption SIGILL / SIGSEGV ... module gogo/protobuf ?
body:
Hi,

Context: Version: RELEASE.2024-03-26T22-10-45Z (go1.21.8 linux/amd64)

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I favor solution depending on supported library so that CVE can be addressed and long term support is more easy.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Minio currently depends on the library gogo/protobuf.
gogo/protobuf is DEPRECATED and no longer maintained. Its last CVE dates from 2021 before its deprecation. Who knows when will be the next one ?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
this seems to be a valid alternative : https://github.com/golang/protobuf
I imagine this is a large rework, but please provide insights : 
- are you currently working on this ? 
- have you an agenda ?
- what is the plan if there is a CVE on this deprecated module ?
- do you have a parent issue reporting all deprecated dependencies ?

Sidenote: 
I found out about this dependency through a segmentation violation error, that is under investigation on my side. We use a minio version from january 2024 so we must update before filling out a bug report.
```
github.com/gogo/protobuf/proto.extensionProperties(0xc114deceb0)
#011github.com/gogo/protobuf@v1.3.2/proto/extensions.go:273 +0x260 fp=0xc11229ee38 sp=0xc11229ed70 pc=0xcd3ea0
runtime: g 9788: unexpected return pc for github.com/gogo/protobuf/proto.extensionProperties called from 0xc1145946e5
stack: frame={sp:0xc11229ed70, fp:0xc11229ee38} stack=[0xc11229e000,0xc11229f000)
0x000000c11229ec70:  0x000000000047db65 <sync.(*Pool).Get+0x0000000000000085>  0x0000000006487ca0
0x000000c11229ec80:  0x00000000064763e0  0x000000000270da40
0x000000c11229ec90:  0x0000000000fdb694 <github.com/minio/minio/internal/grid.readAllInto+0x00000000000000f4>  0x000000c1ae8aefa8
```

Thanks and regards,
JL

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
We do not use protobuf, it is an indirect dependency on MinIO via its other dependencies such as `coredns`. for example etcd has a direct dependency on it.

```
<redacted-host>/etcd/api/v3@v3.5.14 github.com/gogo/protobuf@v1.3.2
```

We cannot fix this on our end.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks for the qui answer, but...

I don't understand why you close the support this fast. 
I think minio is responsible of the dependencies it choose to include !
You said that minio depending on etcd is an issue, can you share the ticket where you are dealing with this issue on the upstream project please ?

Beside, I think that your answer is not accurate.
I think minio uses gogo module in 
https://github.com/minio/minio/blob/1966668066a1f03197c955a870d610c252369a5a/internal/grid/grid.go#L127
through the usage of crypto/tls 
Could you please confirm ?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I think you are referring to this problem of etcd : https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/14533
but as you may notice, the problem is not solve and then the ticket is OPEN.
Please re-open this ticket.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter That looks more like stack/runtime corruption. Your trace has no relation to `gogo/protobuf`.

Try running with `GODEBUG=gcshrinkstackoff=1` as per https://github.com/golang/go/issues/64781

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks Klaus, it seems promising.
Could you please confirm how this config impacts performance ?
I have plenty of headroom on this cluster, but I am also investigating similar issue on a cluster running on HDD which is very overloaded (IOPS starved).

By the way, this particular cluster runs on bare metal server using AMD EPYC 7702P 64-Core Processor so if it's the same bug I confirm it is also occuring on AMD.
OS is Ubuntu Jammy with Kernel 5.15.0-107-generic

I will not be able to make the change anytime soon due to production freeze, but I'll defintely provide information.
Is there any issue regarding this on the minio project ?

comments.body: We tried the `GODEBUG=gcshrinkstackoff=1` option with no success. Still the same SIGILL error

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Are you still using this old version? If so, please upgrade and post a "fresh" stack trace if it happens on the new as well.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Yes we'll do that ASAP. Minio is restarting every 15 minutes on this particular node.
What we cannot understand is how 1 node have this problem and the 7 other nodes of this cluster do not have this issue at all.

In the meantime, on this faulty node we completely disbled GC with `GOGC=off` + we disabled swap so that minio reboot predictibly every ~1 hour.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Follow-up `GOGC=off` was not satisfying because at some point Linux OOM decided to also kill other process than minio and completely crash the whole server (this server is dedicated to minio).

We then fall back to using : `GOGC=off` and `GOMEMLIMIT=128GiB` which is a lot more satisfying.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter Let us know if upgrade helps.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Since we don't understand why this server suffers from the problem and not the 7 other identicals servers from this clusters we tried to re-masterize the server (keeping the minio data untouched) and it had no effect on the issue.

Minio upgrade is in the plan before end of august.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Ok we finally solve it and it had nothing to do with minio.
The problem was that the HPE workload profile on this server was improperly set to "Virtualization - Power Efficient".
We change it to "HPC" as it was on other servers and it solves the issue.

I did not check the exact impact of this settings but it probably wraps the CPU scaling governor settings.
